rejected: Interests flag (reader 10, missed item on p. 604): the link between the two authors' consulting for Cambridge Cognition and a stop-signal implementation rests on the reader's background knowledge; the paper names no implementation and does not connect the consulting to this study, so the funding and conflict fields are unchanged.
for_senior_author: Confounding domain: reader 10 proposes high (smoking more common in the sibling pairs than in the volunteers and checked only for grey matter, pp. 602-603; other substances, sex and education not reported). The overall rating (high) is the same either way; the domain rating is left as in the first pass.

Interpretation gap: substantial is agreed. The reader would add that the authors' own text links lower FA to longer stimulant use (p. 602, 5th paragraph), which qualifies the vulnerability-marker reading; whether to widen the gap text is left to the senior author.

Measurement of the exposure domain: reader 10 proposes some-concerns (a hospital diagnosis recorded at the index admission, before the outcome; misclassification mostly non-differential and toward the null). The overall rating (high) is unchanged either way; the domain rating is left as in the first pass.

Interpretation gap: minor is agreed. The reader notes two small widenings not recorded in the gap text (the Discussion restates the hazard ratio as a 76% increase without the hospital qualifier; the appendicitis cohort is called a population-based sample, p. 38). Left for the senior author.

The added reporting issue on the type of hazard ratio rests on the editors' background knowledge that the crrSC package fits Fine-Gray models; the paper does not name the model. The card says so, and the senior author should confirm it.

The reporting issue on the numbers excluded (p. 36) cites a Utah comparison (Curtin et al., 2015) from outside this PDF; neither reader nor adjudicator could check it. It needs checking against that paper.

rejected: Whether reference 57 (Kalant and Kalant) is a review: the reference list gives only its title, so the card's review label can be neither confirmed nor rejected; left unchanged.
for_senior_author: Interpretation gap: minor is agreed for the review as a whole, but the reader notes that for a Parkinson's disease claim the gap would be substantial (the abstract sentence on p. 1085 against the thin support on p. 1093). Consider a claim-specific gap; not changed.

Interpretation gap: minor is agreed. The reader notes that the main invitation to read the ratio as a risk is the Results wording that 11.2% had progressed to develop dependence (p. 255), while the authors define the ratio as lifetime prevalence among people who have used (p. 248). Optional note for the gap text; no disagreement.

rejected: Reader 10's wording that the Discussion states outright that methamphetamine causes the reduction (p. 1210): the sentence is hedged (a suggestion, with the small sample acknowledged), so the added reporting issue says suggested, not stated.
for_senior_author: Selection of the reported result domain: reader 10 proposes some-concerns (null results are reported next to significant ones; the unreported rate-constant comparisons and the prefrontal data not shown are the concern). The overall rating (high) is unchanged either way; the domain rating is left as in the first pass.

Interpretation gap: substantial is agreed and the reader says the card understates it. The causal sentence (p. 1210) and the predictive-value and Parkinson's-risk statements (p. 1212) are now recorded as a reporting issue, but the claimed text of the gap itself is not extended; left for the senior author.

rejected: Tobacco selection effect (reader 11, missed item): the card already records that every participant smoked tobacco and continued to, and it flags uncontrolled urine pH; the reader's links to urine pH and to familiarity with inhalation are inference and are not in the paper, so nothing was added.
for_senior_author: Replication timeline entry dated 2008: it cannot be checked against this source (its reference list ends in 2003) and needs checking against another source before the card leaves first-pass.

rejected: Amphetamine half-life after 0.5 mg/kg l-methamphetamine (Table I, 43.6 with SD 24.9 and interval 25.8 to 61.4; reader 11, missed item): the interval is centred on the mean and its half-width fits about 10 participants, and several amphetamine half-life intervals in the table fit 7 to 11 participants, as expected when the half-life cannot be estimated in everyone. Not an error; not added (the AUC interval for 0.25 mg/kg l-methamphetamine was confirmed and added).

Paragraph numbers for the Subjective measures text (reader: 2nd and 3rd): the l-methamphetamine versus placebo sentence is in the 1st paragraph, so the locator reads 1st to 2nd; the page correction (p. 410 alone) was accepted.
for_senior_author: Sixth RoB 2 domain: the card uses a crossover-specific domain, period and carryover effects, which the five-domain parallel-group version of RoB 2 does not have (the crossover variant does); neither METHODS nor rob_vocab.py names it. Decide whether to keep it as its own domain or fold it into randomization. The reader agreed with its rating, as with all domains and the overall some-concerns.

Interpretation gap: substantial is agreed; the reader says the strongest ground is the step from single intravenous doses in 12 men to abuse liability of a market supply and toxicity under repeated dosing (pp. 418-419). Gap text not changed.

rejected: Heart-rate P values of 0.032 and 0.036 (p. 128; reader 11, missed item): these belong to two different tests (the dose effect and the pairwise comparison with placebo), and the Discussion's P<0.036 covers diastolic pressure (0.003) and heart rate (0.036); not an inconsistency, so not added.
Reader's placement of the oral-fluid sentence in the 3rd paragraph of Windows of detection: it is the 2nd (the 3rd begins with the SAMHSA cutoffs); the locator now names the 1st and 2nd paragraphs.
Reader's placement of the Discussion values K01 0.93 and K10 0.085 per hour on p. 129: they are on p. 128 (p. 129 holds only Figure 3); the page is corrected to pp. 125, 128.
for_senior_author: Instrument question: a fixed-order, subject-blind administration study with no randomization or counterbalancing is appraised with RoB 2 only because the design enum maps human-laboratory to it. Either document the exception on the card or re-appraise with ROBINS-I (reader 11 agrees with high overall and with every domain).

rejected: Context for the 90.3% figure (reader 11, missed item: the in-vitro syringe experiment, 57.0% trapped vapour and 44.8% left in the device, p. 718): already covered by key finding 0 and by the denominator problem now in the reporting issues, and the experiment does not describe people; not added.

The reader's estimate that a reader would be out by about a third when taking the urinary percentages against the amount placed in the device is not carried over, because it depends on assumptions about that amount.
for_senior_author: Instrument question, same as Schepers 2003: no order, allocation or washout is described, so this is not a randomized or counterbalanced design and RoB 2 is applied only because the design enum maps human-laboratory to it. Document the exception on the card or re-appraise with ROBINS-I (reader 11 agrees with high overall and with every domain).
